solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not against South American capital going into cereal

indicators.note: Not tells us the word for against is to be left out of the capital

parts.note: Santiago is the capital of Chile
anti means against

explanation.surface: Someone who isn't opposed to a Latin American city switching to breakfast grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' takes ANTI out of SANTIAGO, leaving the starch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy grain-like food from palm pith, loosely grouped with cereals and puddings.

clue.text: Second choice could be not including torpedo boat in retreat

indicators.note: in places the abbreviations inside the word for a retreat

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway
ex means without, as in ex dividend

explanation.surface: A fallback plan that leaves out the warship during a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' suggests a reversal, but retreat is NEST, the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The option ranked just below the top one is the runner-up preference.

clue.text: Espy state secret concealed in part of compositor's gear

indicators.note: concealed asks for the letters to be disguised, i.e. rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A spy's state secret is smuggled inside printing equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor sets metal type by hand, taking letters from a divided tray kept for that trade.

clue.text: Old boy's forgotten by couple of masters — jerks!

indicators.note: forgotten by says the old boy drops out of the couple of masters

parts.note: beak is British slang for a schoolmaster, so a couple of masters is two beaks
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil overlooked by two teachers calls them idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: The O comes out of TWO and the B out of BEAKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweaks as a verb means quick sharp pulls or twitches, the same as jerks.

clue.text: 9 Lord Lieutenant's drawing constituent's joint boundaries

indicators.note: drawing here means being drawn in, so the next pieces go inside the word for constituents

parts.note: parts are constituents, with the 's giving the plural S
9 across is the instruction to shuffle the word for road, way, here giving YWA
LL is the abbreviation for Lord Lieutenant

explanation.surface: A county's Lord Lieutenant draws up shared property lines for a voter.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across, WAY OUT, works throughout as an anagram of WAY ('out' signalling the shuffle).
explanation.definitionFit: A party wall is one shared between two adjoining properties, so these are shared borders.

clue.text: Oscar's a wag, holding a brief rally near 9

indicators.note: holding says the word for a wag contains what follows

parts.note: a card is a joker or wag
a demo is a protest rally; cut short it gives DEM
9 across is the instruction to shuffle the word for road, way, here giving YAW

explanation.surface: A joker clutching a protest banner near the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' just places the shuffled WAY beside DEM. 9 across, WAY OUT, works as an anagram of WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is the statuette given by the film industry's Academy for achievement.

clue.text: See 6 across
9 races for Sir Thomas

parts.note: 9 across is the instruction to shuffle the word for road, way, here giving WYA
the TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Bizarre races staged for a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across, WAY OUT, works as an anagram of WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor poet Sir Thomas Wyatt introduced the sonnet into English.

clue.text: Wrote on composition notes in order to produce serial music

definitions.text: notes in order to produce serial music

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A composer wrote on a score, setting down notes in order for twelve-tone music.
explanation.definitionFit: In serialism the composer fixes a sequence of the twelve pitches that the piece then follows.

clue.text: Very unusual vomitory

definitions.meaning: a vomitory is an exit passage from a stadium or amphitheatre

explanation.surface: A bizarre exit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both informal for eccentric and a plain term for an exit, the sense of an arena's vomitory.

clue.text: Passing time among returning staff starts to impress new guys

indicators.note: among puts the time abbreviation in with the other letters
returning says the word for staff is read backwards

parts.note: a cane is a walking staff

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: As time passes, returning staff start to impress new colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' is a law being passed, not time going by. The blogger found 'among' loose, as the T sits between the two parts rather than inside one.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament passing a bill is enacting it, making it law.

clue.text: Qualities evenly incorporated in an outfit for Madame Bovary, perhaps?

indicators.note: incorporated in puts the selected letters inside the garment

parts.note: a dress is an outfit

indicators.note: evenly takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Emma Bovary's qualities shown through her costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's heroine is an example of a wife who is unfaithful to her husband.

clue.text: Shaggy cap worn by Rumpole?

definitions.meaning: the shaggy ink cap is a mushroom with a hairy white cap, also called by this legal name
Rumpole of the Bailey is a fictional barrister, so his headgear is the courtroom wig

explanation.surface: An unkempt hat sported by a fictional barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a common name for the shaggy ink cap fungus and the horsehair headpiece of a barrister.

clue.text: Faded piece of scrimshaw ornamentation

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Decoration carved on whalebone that has dulled with age.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn has lost its freshness through use, as faded colours have.

clue.text: Fight two whole rounds — or take it as it comes?

indicators.note: rounds suggests the letters are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer chooses between battling the full distance and simply accepting fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for accepting events passively rather than resisting them.

clue.text: Diplomatic action from Georgia certain to involve Turkish leader

parts.note: GE is the international code for Georgia

indicators.note: to involve says the word for certain wraps round the leader's letter

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of Turkish

explanation.surface: A Georgian diplomatic move sure to bring in a Turkish head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A goodwill move or token made between states is a symbolic diplomatic act.

clue.text: Thinly snick to 9 — 'Not out this time, son'

parts.note: in cricket a snick is a thin edge off the bat

indicators.note: Not says the word out is dropped from 9 across

parts.note: the 9 refers to the entry at 9 across

explanation.surface: A batsman edges a ball and is told he was not out this time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this time' marks the one place where the 9 across entry is used as written, minus OUT, rather than as an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned edgeways an object presents its narrowest side, so it appears thin.

clue.text: Man conceivably setter will sound out

indicators.note: sound out says the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the setter is I, so setter will is I'll

explanation.surface: A man might imagine a crossword compiler testing opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is one example of an island, hence 'conceivably'.

clue.text: Retail outlet where car boot may be handy?

definitions.text: Retail outlet where car boot may be handy?

parts.words: Retail outlet where car boot may be handy?
parts.note: a car boot sale is a British market of used goods sold from car trunks; here the boot belongs in a domestic car shelter

explanation.surface: A shop where car boot space comes in handy.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling unwanted goods from one's own car shed or driveway is a small one-off market.

clue.text: Glance from scruffy gendarme put setter off

indicators.note: scruffy suggests a messed-up state, so the letters are jumbled
put ... off tells us to remove the setter from the jumbled letters
off, with put, signals taking the setter's pronoun away

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A grubby French policeman discouraged the crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a gander is slang for having a quick look.

clue.text: Draw a parallel with some people's pronounced skin problem?

indicators.note: pronounced says the word is heard, and some people's admits only some speakers say it that way

parts.note: lichen is a skin disease with small raised spots

explanation.surface: Comparing how people say the name of a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare one thing to another is to draw a parallel between them.

clue.text: Relatively slow U-boats laid up unfinished

parts.note: U-boats are German submarines, subs

indicators.note: unfinished cuts off the last letter

parts.note: something laid up or shelved is on ice

explanation.surface: Submarines in dock, half-built, which aren't fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeds below the speed of sound are slow compared with supersonic ones.

clue.text: Scribbler with nothing about him makes whoopee

indicators.note: about says the letters for with and nothing go round the writer

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a hack is a jobbing writer, a scribbler

explanation.surface: A writer surrounded by nothing has a wild party.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated British exclamations of delight, interchangeable as cries of joy.

clue.text: Long and hard serve is crushing

indicators.note: crushing means squeezing in, so the serve holds the letter

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable tennis serve
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A long, hard tennis serve is overpowering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb here, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn or pine for something is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Members of panel I'd eagerly cut short

indicators.note: Members of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Panel members eagerly cutting a speaker off.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a sound or syllable, merging words, is to abbreviate speech.

clue.text: Tell me to stop hens straying round 9

indicators.note: round says the shuffled birds go around the other letters
straying means the letters wander out of order

parts.note: 9 across is the instruction to shuffle the word for road, way, here giving AYW

explanation.surface: A farmer asks to be told when to stop the hens wandering around the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: As in every themed clue, 9 across (WAY OUT) means 'an anagram of WAY'; here both shuffles interleave.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when pouring a drink, asking the other person to signal enough.
